newsitem.title: UK: BP, Shell off after ADR falls.
newsitem.headline: BP, Shell off after ADR falls.

text.p: Shares in British Petroleum Co Plc and Shell Transport & Trading Co Plc dropped in pre-market trade on Tuesday, echoing declines in their ADRs in New York yesterday and ahead of year-end results from the two oil giants.
Dealers said recent weakness in oil prices had encouraged a bout of profit-taking after the sharp gains both stocks have seen through the past year.
BP was down 14p at 707 by 0804 GMT after its ADRs dropped $3-7/8 to 138-5/8, while Shell was down 12-1/2p at 10.56-1/2 stg after its ADRs fell $2 to $175-3/4.
Enterprise Oil, which almost doubled in price through 1996 to reach a record 698p on January 31, was also marked lower to be down 12p at 660-1/2. Lasmo Plc was down 7-1/2p at 246-1/2.
BP is later today expected to post a rise in replacement cost net profit before one-off items to between 2.50 billion stg and 2.75 billion, up from 2.01 billion a year before.
Royal Dutch Shell on Wednesday is expected to report profits on the same measure of between 5.14 billion stg and 5.50 billion, up from 4.52 billion.

"We have seen a steady pullback in oil prices and the feeling is growing that we have got sufficient inventories in the western world to cope with any late cold snap," said one dealer. "And the stocks have all had a good run."

Yesterday Merrill Lynch cut its rating on Enterprise to "reduce" from "neutral", pointing out that the stock was trading at a hefty 45 percent premium to its net asset value and could gradually come back to around the 600p level as bid speculation wanes.
